Documentation · All releases

Project Looking Glass 1.69.0

Released 2026-10-22 · GitHub release · CHANGELOG.md

1.69.0 — 2026-10-22 — Gradle / JDK 21 modernization

Added

  • QNX-style process isolation, Phase 1: the child-process app framework and the Web Browser as its first isolated app (lg3d-core, org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d; lg3d-apps, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webbrowser) — The combined launch (run-lg3d.sh --iso) already boots the 2D desktop and the X11 WM/compositor in one JVM so a foreign X window can be redirected into an MDI frame; this adds the other half — running an *application* in its own OS process so a native crash, an OOM or a System.exit in the app can never take the desktop JVM down. Desktop2DAppRegistry.Kind gains CHILD_PROCESS (a java <class> command forked into an isolated JVM rather than constructed in-process), backed by a new CHILD_PROCESS_APPS table and childMainClass. ChildProcessLauncher builds the isolated command line (this JVM's own launcher + classpath, a bounded -Xmx512m, the software Prism pipeline with HiDPI pinned off, and the WebKit compositing/DMABUF workarounds) and its environment over the privacy-critical Tor proxy env — pure builders, so they are asserted without forking a JVM. AppProcessSupervisor owns one live child per app: a second launch raises the running child instead of re-forking, output is drained, and a bounded restart policy (decide) turns an exit into relaunch / relaunch-on-a-fresh-budget / stop-clean / give-up, so a crash recovers on its own and never loops forever. Desktop2D.openApp routes CHILD_PROCESS through launchChildProcessApp, and the file-association launcher treats it like a frame app. The Web Browser — a native WebKit/OpenGL surface and the single most likely thing in the desktop to hard-crash — is the reference migration: it moves out of PANEL_APPS into CHILD_PROCESS_APPS (forking WebBrowserApp), and WebBrowserApp hardens the child (a default uncaught-exception handler exits non-zero so the supervisor sees the crash; Platform.setImplicitExit(false) hands JVM lifetime to the Swing windowClosed handler). Under --iso the compositor redirects the child's window back into an MDI frame, so the browser is both isolated *and* integrated; on a plain 2D desktop it appears as its own window. Covered headlessly by ChildProcessLauncherTest, AppProcessSupervisorTest, the updated Desktop2DAppRegistryTest and the new process-isolation.feature Cucumber scenarios; the live window/compositor behaviour is validated on a bare Xorg host (see docs/lfs-iso-contract.md).
  • QNX-style process isolation, Phases 2 & 3: the generic panel host, config inheritance and graceful reaping (lg3d-core, org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.desktop2d; lg3d-apps, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.host) — Phase 1 isolated exactly one bespoke child (the Web Browser, which needs JavaFX hardening). Phase 2 generalises that into a *mechanism* so isolating an ordinary Swing app needs no per-app code, and Phase 3 makes the desktop clean up after the children it forked. ChildProcessLauncher gains a ChildProfile (BROWSER / SWING) that selects the heap, the JavaFX Prism pipeline and the WebKit environment per app, and — the piece that made a forked child unable to find its resources — lgSystemPropertyArgs(), which propagates the desktop's lg.* / lg3d.* system properties (plus a jar-path and logging allow-list) to the child as -D arguments, since a forked JVM does not inherit them. New PanelHostApp (lg3d-apps) is the generic isolated-panel host: a child main that reflectively builds any leaf Swing panel via Desktop2DAppRegistry.createPanelByClassName and shows it in its own frame, exiting the process when the frame closes so the supervisor sees a clean stop; its argument parsing and title derivation are pure and headless-tested, only main and the frame assembly touch a display (so it lives in lg3d-apps, reached from core by class-name string with no compile dependency). The registry now models a child as a ChildTarget (main class + args + profile) and exposes childArgs, childProfile, panelHostMain and panelHostArgs, so Desktop2D.newChildSupervisor derives the profile, JVM arguments, environment and restart policy from the registry — isolating a new app is a one-line registration, not a change to the launcher. AppProcessSupervisor gains Policy.swing() (two retries over a 10 s stable window) and, in Phase 3, a shutdown() that terminates the live child and suppresses both its restart and its stop notification (a teardown is not a crash); Desktop2D.exit() reaps every forked child through it, so logging out leaves no orphaned java process. A panel is not flipped to CHILD_PROCESS blindly — that is a live-only decision gated on the bare-Xorg runbook (docs/lfs-iso-contract.md §4, criteria 5–6), which is why this delivers the covered mechanism rather than migrating a working in-JVM panel. Extended ChildProcessLauncherTest, Desktop2DAppRegistryTest, AppProcessSupervisorTest (shutdown) and the new PanelHostAppTest, plus three further process-isolation.feature scenarios (generic panel host, Swing-child config inheritance, graceful reaping).
  • Tetris, the Games group's fifth game and its first written for both desktops at once (lg3d-apps, org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.games.tetris; lg3d-core, lg3d-art) — The four existing *Games* entries are incubator apps that were built as native-3D boards first and given a Swing panel afterwards, so each ships an AWT-free model, a live-texture view, a Frame3D host and a panel that duplicates the view's constants to avoid loading Java 3D in the 2D JVM. Tetris goes the other way: one plain-Swing game, hosted. Tetris.main installs the hosted Metal LAF and hands TetrisPanel to TitledSwingWindow.show(...) for the 3D desktop — the Calculator pattern — and the *same* descriptor (tetris.lgcfg, Games, icon resources/images/icon/tetris.png) launches it in the 2D/Swing desktop because the wrapper class is now a key in Desktop2DAppRegistry.PANEL_APPS mapping to TetrisPanel, which therefore keeps a no-arg constructor and never touches a Java 3D class. The well, the seven pieces, the ghost drop target and the PAUSED / GAME OVER overlays are all custom-painted, so the game ships no sprite. Input is the interesting difference: the four 3D games are click-driven because dev mode routes no keyboard focus to a Frame3D, but SwingNodeRenderer redispatches real KeyEvents at a component, so the panel's focusable board carries the only KeyListener (arrows move, Up/X rotate, Down soft-drops, Space hard-drops, P pauses, and Enter starts a run *only* when none is on the board) while the sidebar buttons are setFocusable(false) so the board keeps the keys — the path both surfaces share, and the reason this game plays identically in either desktop. A five-button pad (Rotate, Left, Down, Right, Drop) is the mouse twin of those keys, calling the very same engine methods through the same turn handler, so a host that never gives the board keyboard focus still has a playable game. TetrisEngine holds the rules with no Swing and no timer (the panel owns the clock): 40/100/300/1200 × level per 1/2/3/4 lines, a level every ten rows that shortens the fall delay down to a clamped 50 ms floor, and a piece generator injectable as a Random so a test can pin the sequence without seed hunting. Making *reset* and *losing* different states was a real fix found by reading: stopping the clock alone left the last piece on a cleared grid, which isGameOver() (a piece present, no run, no pause) reads as a lost game — so a board the player had just reset painted GAME OVER over an empty well, and start() and stop() now both go through atRest(); only a lock that has nowhere to put a piece ends a run. Twelve WAV clips are bundled at the package path by lg3d-apps' existing resource source set (~1.1 MB); the ported original's 33 MB victory jingle and every file no effect plays are not shipped — a released jar is weight a user downloads to play a game — and TetrisAudio loads each clip lazily and degrades to silence on a machine with no mixer, because a missing clip is otherwise indistinguishable from a soundless machine. Sound on/off, volume and starting speed persist through java.util.prefs (TetrisSettings), clamped on read so a hand-edited store cannot ask for a negative fall delay, and the form that edits them is a JOptionPane confirm dialog parented to the panel — the pattern 47 other hosted lg3d-apps panels already rely on, viable on the 3D desktop because SwingNodeWindowCapture parks a hosted app's dialog off-screen and paints it as a centred overlay into the node's own texture, modal input included. The icon is generated, not hand-placed: GenerateAppIcons.java gains an in-tool TetrisStack glyph (a settled stack with a gap, one piece still falling) on the deep-purple tile no other icon in that table generates. Documented in the Help Center's application inventory (apps.html Games table, start-menu.html, and desktop-2d.html, which said *four* games), in a per-app AGENTS.md carrying the Production status row, and proven by 53 headless JUnit 5 cases (TetrisEngineTest 18, TetrisPanelTest 14, TetrisAudioTest 8, TetrominoTest 7, TetrisSettingsTest 6 — the two settings-bound suites over a unique throwaway preferences node each, removed in @AfterEach, because the test JVM does not isolate java.util.prefs) plus Desktop2DAppRegistryTest.tetrisIsHostedPanel; TetrisAudioTest compares the shipped files against the effects as one explicit set, which is the gate that keeps "an effect nobody bundled" from becoming a sound nobody hears. The 3D surface was then run, not assumed: the in-JVM probe recipe (:lg3d-core:run -Pwindowed -PswingApp=…) mounted the panel in a live Frame3D and the internal screencapture showed the glassy "Tetris" window with a piece falling, its ghost on the floor and the next piece queued — and it caught two defects no headless test could see: every scoreboard row painted its caption twice ("Score: Score: 0", because fieldRow adds the caption and the value label repeated it) and the control pad's rotate button read "Rot..." at the sidebar's first width. Both are fixed, both fixes are now pinned by the two added TetrisPanelTest cases (a row's caption must not reappear in its own value; no control may be narrower than it asks to be), and the re-capture shows the corrected labels. ./gradlew build green across every module (tests + JaCoCo floors) and :lg3d-mandela:repositoryChecks green over all sixteen gates, with startMenuAudit now listing 5 items in Games and "every live descriptor resolves"; the *What's New* topic and the Pages release archive were regenerated from this changelog in the same PR.
  • ui-strings.mnd — a Mandela report on the screen text that never asks the bundle (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — i18n-keys.mnd can only audit the keys a source *asks* for, and Messages.tr() degrades safely — a missing key echoes the key — so a label that skips the bundle is not an error at build time or at runtime either: it is simply English, forever, and nothing in the repository counted how many there are. The report reads the one piece of evidence a source gives: a string literal written into the argument slot of a widget constructor, a text setter, a JOptionPane message (the *second* argument, after the parent component) or a panel's own status helper, and prints it beside the slot that asks the bundle instead — per module, per surface, and ranked per file, so the output is the schedule a person works through rather than a list of violations. Its 21-name vocabulary was measured before it was written down, and three families were left out on evidence rather than taste: 32 of 32 error( and all 183 info( sites, and 71 of 90 warn( sites, carry a LOG./log./logger. receiver, so their argument is a log line and not a label; Container.add("…") is a desktop-entry section header or a diagnostic collected into a list; and JMenu/setTipText have no literal call site at all. Four buckets are defined in the header, because a grep and a report must not be read as disagreeing: prose, single word ("OK", "#ff0000", a value or a label, and only a reader can tell), blank (a spaces-only new JLabel(" ") is a spacer no translator would ship) and excluded (a path the module's own build file leaves out renders for nobody). Its first run read 2,842 sources and counted 1,314 prose literals against 20 bundle lookups: lg3d-apps carries 1,178 of them and lg3d-core 12, because the shell is the half that was made translatable, and the schedule starts at DockerManagementPanel (74), MessengerPanel (55) and VideoConferencePanel (52). Every number was checked against an independent grep pass — the source count and each surface count exact, or explained by two calls on one line, and the 20 lookups exact — and that check found two defects in the report itself, both fixed here: the three JOptionPane names were in the dialog list but not in the vocabulary, so the 40 dialog messages it now counts were invisible, and the cheap per-line gate tested for a quote, which hid a lookup built from data (subMenu.setToolTipText(Messages.trLgcfgDesc(child.getName(), …))) until gate and classifier were made to read one marker list. 37 legacy Latin-1 sources do not decode as text and are named, the same blind spot i18n-keys.mnd reports. It is a report, not a gate — it always exits 0 and is wired as :lg3d-mandela:uiStrings, deliberately outside repositoryChecks, because a literal in a constructor is a screen to translate and not a defect — documented in the scripts README.md and in AGENTS.md beside i18n-keys.mnd, the question it answers.
  • help-topics.mnd — a Mandela gate on the Help Center's JavaHelp bundle as one graph (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — The Help Center is javax.help over five hand-written copies of one fact: lg3d-help.hs names the homeID, the map and the three navigators, map.jhm pairs every target with the topic that answers it, toc.xml spells Contents, index.xml spells the keyword index, the 19 topics link each other, the stylesheet and their images by relative path — and HelpContentTest.java re-writes the target list and the file list again as two Java arrays. JavaHelp reports a broken edge by showing nothing: a target the map does not carry is a Contents row that does nothing when a reader clicks it, a topic no mapID names is a page the indexer globs into JavaSearch that no navigator can reach, a homeID the map lacks is a Help Center that opens on a blank pane, and a topic added to the directory but left out of the test's arrays keeps the suite green while the reader never finds it. Nine checks: the build file's own helpContentDir / include '*.html' / into '…/JavaSearch' literals as a *premise*; the HelpSet's homeID, mapref, navigator data and title against HelpCenterPanel's HELPSET_PATH and HOME_ID and the assertion the headless test copies; each target declared once with its url on disk and no topic left unnamed; Contents in both directions; the Index in both directions, with no target-less leaf, no target unreachable by keyword and the alphabetical order index.xml's own comment promises, checked level by level; a <title>, an <h1> and the stylesheet link in every topic; every relative href, src and #fragment resolving against the file or the anchor it names; the Contents label echoing the heading the reader actually lands on, except for overview and whats-new, which are written into the script's LABEL_EXEMPT with their reasons — where an exemption that stops being true is itself the finding, the discipline exclusions.mnd and coverage-floors.mnd apply; and the test's two arrays paired with the map and the directory, both ways. Wired as :lg3d-mandela:helpTopicsCheck inside repositoryChecks (fifteen gates become sixteen). It ships green over 19 targets, 108 index entries and 117 relative links with no defect to report, so what it records is one judgement instead: help/resources/images/lg3d-wm-usage.de.png is named by no topic and no source, printed and never failed, because only a reader knows whether a translation is pending or the file is dead weight in the jar. Proven by planting 20 defects and reverting each — the premise literal moved, a mapID url aimed at a missing file, a target declared twice, an undeclared target in Contents and in the Index, a target no keyword reaches, an index leaf with neither target nor children, an entry out of alphabetical order, a topic that stopped linking the stylesheet, a dead #fragment, a dead image src, a topic with no <title>, a Contents label the page does not carry, a label exemption that no longer holds, a homeID the map does not declare, the panel's HOME_ID and HELPSET_PATH drifted, the HelpSet title drifted from the assertion, a navigator's data file missing, a target dropped from TARGETS — each naming the file it found. Writing it also corrected a defect in the gate itself: its tag walker advanced its consumed offset by the distance to > but not by the length of the tag name, which slid every later indent back by ten characters and made the two nesting-dependent checks report two false gaps on a bundle that had none.
  • branch-hygiene.mnd — a Mandela report on which branches are left on one side of this repository (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — AGENTS.md states the rule twice: a merge is not finished until the branch is gone from both sides, because a stale local that outlives its merged PR is how a later commit lands on a dead branch and comes back cherry-picked under a second SHA. The check today is a human remembering to type git branch --merged, git cherry and gh pr list, and none of that is visible to a compiler or a CI step. But git keeps its own answer in files — a branch *is* a one-line text file under .git/refs/heads/, a remote-tracking branch is the same under refs/remotes/origin/, and packed-refs holds the folded ones with the loose file winning, since git repacks lazily and the packed copy still names the tip a branch had *before* its last commit. So the report reads exactly what git reads, which is also the only option: the language reserves a PROCESS grant it has no function for, so no Mandela script can spawn git even to try. Five sections — the checked-out branch (and a detached HEAD, the one case where a commit belongs to no ref at all), locals with no origin/ counterpart, locals whose tip *is* origin/main's tip and therefore provably carry no unique work without asking the object graph, two local names on one commit (the cherry-pick signature), and origin/ entries no local holds. It is a report and not a gate, wired as :lg3d-mandela:branchHygiene and deliberately outside repositoryChecks: refs prove existence and SHA equality and never *ancestry*, so the script prints git fetch --prune, git cherry and gh pr list beside its own numbers instead of calling an entry a defect, and says twice that refs/remotes/origin is a cache correct only as of the last fetch — the reason a merged PR can still look alive here. Its first run named 9 local-only branches and 4 origin/ entries; verified by hand, GitHub carries only 3 heads (so 3 of those 4 are cache for already-merged PRs), origin/feat/wonderland-p32-gpu-bloom is MERGED yet still on the remote — --delete-branch was not applied — and git cherry gives 8 of the 9 locals unique commits, 5 of them from closed PRs which must not be pruned, leaving exactly one (feat/release-notes-and-site, 0 unique commits, PR #378 merged) as the stale local the rule warns about. Documented in the scripts README.md and in AGENTS.md, both under *Branch hygiene is part of merging*.
  • gate-new.mnd — a Mandela generator that scaffolds the next gate in the shape the shipped ones already have (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — fifteen gates in scripts/mandela share five parts, and the two a person forgets are not the syntax: ShippedScriptsTest already pins the shebang, the // name.mnd — what it is for line and an invocation that names -s, so what rots is the *premise* — the check that fails loudly when the file a gate reads its answer from has moved, without which a vanished authority is reported as a clean tree — and the prose paragraph that says why the two surfaces can drift and what the mismatch costs a user. gate-new.mnd my-check writes scripts/mandela/my-check.mnd with all of that in place, derives the Gradle task name from the same word (my-check → myCheckCheck, so nobody is asked to invent a second name for one tool), cleans a sloppy argument the way deck-new.mnd does (My_Bad Name_.mnd → my-bad-name) and refuses to overwrite a gate someone may already be editing. It is a generator, not a gate: it writes the one file and *prints* the three edits it deliberately does not make — the mandelaCheck(...) registration, its repositoryChecks entry and the README row — because a tool that rewrote lg3d-mandela/build.gradle would have scripts-hygiene.mnd auditing its own work rather than the author's, and that gate is exactly what goes red while a scaffold sits unwired. Proven end to end on this tree: the generated file compiled under the same check the build runs, ran green, then failed with exit 2 once its AUTHORITY was pointed at a file that does not exist, and leaving it unwired produced the single scripts-hygiene finding its own header promises. Documented in the scripts README.md (including in *Adding a script*, which now starts from the scaffold) and in AGENTS.md beside the two generators of its kind.
  • bgconfigs.mnd — a Mandela gate on the Background Manager's menu against the art the tree ships (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — One flat list, bgmanager/res/BgConfig.xml, names every background by a resources/Backgrounds/<Name>/LgBgConf.lgbg classpath URL, each .lgbg names its thumbnail and its panorama faces the same way, and :lg3d-core:runtimeResources relocates the whole tree under the top-level resources/ prefix — that spelling is the only one the classloader lookup accepts. Two SAX readers sit at the end of that chain and neither is forgiving: BgConfigFileReader throws Wrong tag on any element but <BgManagerConfig>/<BGURL> and appends every URL without de-duplicating, and BgFileReader throws Undefined Tag on anything outside its thirteen names, so one stray element is not one lost background but a stack trace and an empty picker, while one repeated URL silently offers the same panorama twice. None of it is visible to the compiler, and all of it is visible in the files. Eight checks: only the elements the config reader knows (plus no < followed by whitespace, which SAX rejects before any element is read), no duplicated <BGURL>, every URL naming a descriptor that exists, every descriptor named by a URL, every directory under Backgrounds/ holding one, every element of every .lgbg inside BgFileReader's own vocabulary, the required elements present with a BGType among the three it compares against and numbers Integer and Float can actually parse, and every resources/… image reference resolving through the mapping — which the script reads back from lg3d-core/build.gradle as a *premise*, so the day the task stops relocating those directories the gate says so instead of enforcing a rule the build no longer applies. Wired as :lg3d-mandela:bgConfigsCheck inside repositoryChecks (fourteen gates become fifteen); the two defects its first run found are the *Fixed* entry below. Green at 48 <BGURL> entries, 48 directories and 48 descriptors in exact agreement with 173 image references resolving, and proven by planting an unknown element, a < with a space after it, a descriptor no <BGURL> names, a missing <Name>, a fourth BGType value and an unresolvable image path — each one fails.
  • exclusions.mnd — a Mandela gate that the exclusion set in the prose is the exclusion set in the build (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — this file's *Code Exclusions* and *Incubator Exclusions* sections name the code paths the build leaves out, and every module's build.gradle writes the same fact again as exclude 'org/…' lines inside a java source set. Nothing made the two agree, and the document admitted the gap itself ("it has been stale before"): an exclude no prose explains is a reader who restores the tree and inherits its JDK 21 defect blind, and a prose token no build applies promises an exclusion for sources that are already compiled into the jar. The gate reads both surfaces, pairs them on *path segments* rather than strings — so sun/** explains sun.awt.*, apps/browser/** explains the build's own spelling, and apps/browser/** provably never matches apps/browser3d/** — and checks the "Ported, not excluded" claim against the same set. It also asks whether a pattern still names a tree: that found one real dead exclude, org/jdesktop/lg3d/apps/x11integration/**, inherited from the 2006 build.xml and repeated in four documents, over a package that has no sources anywhere in the repository or anywhere in its git history; the line stays as the guard that keeps a restored legacy tree out, recorded with that reason in the script's KEPT map — the same discipline run-classpath.mnd and legacy-j3d.mnd apply to a deliberate absence, where an entry that stops being true is itself a finding. Wired as :lg3d-mandela:exclusionsCheck in repositoryChecks; green over 14 exclude(s) paired 1:1 with 14 prose tokens, and proven by planting an undocumented exclude, a deleted one the prose still claims and an exclude on a ported app, which fail as 5 findings in one run.
  • run-classpath.mnd — a Mandela gate on the two hand-written copies of the desktop classpath (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — :lg3d-core:run assembles its classpath by hand — module jars plus a dozen detached configurations — because the desktop launches start-menu apps *in its own JVM* and a Maven dependency of lg3d-apps never reaches that JVM on its own; releaseBundle then writes the same list a second time, because the released launcher runs -cp "${HERE}/lib/*" and a jar absent from lib/ is simply not on the released desktop's classpath. Two hand-written copies of one truth is the defect this port has now hit three times (OpenJFX, POI, JNA): an app that works under ./gradlew :lg3d-core:run and dies with NoClassDefFoundError on the user's machine. The script reads lg3d-core/build.gradle twice and settings.gradle once, then runs seven checks in both directions — the module jars each side carries, a jar shipped outside lib/ must be handed to the dev run by a systemProperty too, every included module is carried somewhere or carries a written reason, the third-party coordinates, the vendored ext/ allow-list (both copies must agree and every jar named must exist, since a misspelled include silently copies nothing), and the run task must depend on every jar it puts on the classpath. It asserts its own premise first: if lib/* stops being the released classpath, the two module checks prove nothing. Wired as :lg3d-mandela:runClasspathCheck inside repositoryChecks; its first run over this tree is the *Fixed* entry below.
  • coverage-floors.mnd — a Mandela gate on what the coverage floors may claim (scripts, lg3d-mandela) — The root coverageFloors map is load-bearing in two directions that nothing checked: check runs jacocoTestCoverageVerification only for a module named there, so a module that gains a suite and no floor is measured but never guarded, while a floor for a module with no suite names a rule that can never fire — protection advertised, not delivered. A suite means at least one .java under src/test/java, because an empty directory makes the Gradle test task NO-SOURCE and JaCoCo never runs; :lg3d-terminal:test was exactly that and no surface said so. A module with a suite and a deliberate exemption must carry its reason in the script the way legacy-j3d.mnd scopes its exemptions, and an exemption that stops being true is itself a finding. A fourth surface is compared: the floors quoted in root AGENTS.md *Test coverage* prose against the map the build enforces, so a bump that leaves the prose behind tells a reader a number nothing guards. Wired as :lg3d-mandela:coverageFloorsCheck; it ships green over 16 floor(s) in 19 module(s) with one documented exemption (lg3d-apps, whose panels are probe-verified against a live desktop), and it was proven in both directions at once by moving lg3d-widgets' floor onto lg3d-terminal, which fails twice in a single run. The two gates together take repositoryChecks from eleven to thirteen and are documented in the scripts README.md and root AGENTS.md — scripts-hygiene.mnd is the gate that named the omission the moment the scripts were committed without their rows.
  • Espresso can now clear the caches Gradle generates for itself, straight from the toolbar (lg3d-apps) — A new *Clear Gradle Cache* toolbar action (gradle-clear-cache) deletes the caches holding what Gradle generates from the project's own build files — caches/<version>/scripts, the tree a cp_proj / cp_settings generic class cache lives in; the instrumented jars (caches/jars-9); and the generated accessor workspaces (caches/<version>/dependencies-accessors, kotlin-dsl) — so a stale one is rebuilt on the next run. It deliberately leaves caches/<version>/modules-2 and the metadata stores in place: wiping a download costs the user a re-fetch of every dependency, and the message the action was first written to answer is more often a JDK/tool mismatch than damaged files (see the *Fixed* entry below), so the scope is what the diagnosis supports and the tooltip says so. One caveat the action states rather than hides: a running daemon keeps a deleted workspace open, so clearing a cache under one answers with *“Could not read workspace metadata from …/metadata.bin”* until gradle --stop releases it — a failure reproduced today, on this repository’s own build, by exactly that sequence. The action reports how many trees it deleted — or that there was nothing to clear — on the status line, and a test seam (setGradleCachesDirForTesting) lets the headless suite prove the delete without touching the real user cache. 3 headless cases in GradleBuildToolsTest: a fake cache holding a cp_proj tree, a dependencies-accessors metadata tree, an instrumented-jar tree and a dependency jar — the first three go, the last is asserted kept, and the answer names the daemon; a dependency-only root that must not be touched at all; and a missing cache directory that reports nothing to clear without creating one.
  • Espresso now provisions each project's own build tool and manages JDKs centrally — a hermetic Gradle/Maven toolchain per project, a shared multi-JDK manager (lg3d-apps) — Creating a project used to scaffold only src/Main.java + README.md and then build it with whatever gradle/mvn happened to be on PATH, so a project carrying its own Gradle distribution still reported "Gradle is not available". Espresso is now hermetic per project and central for JDKs. Per project, the *New Project…* form (ProjectCard) collects a NewProjectRequest — a name, a build system (Gradle / Maven / plain Java), that tool's version and a JDK selected from the manager — and the host provisions it off the EDT on a virtual thread (AdvancedTextEditorPanel.provisionNewProject → ProjectProvisioner) with status-line progress: it refuses a non-empty directory, scaffolds the sources, README.md, .gitignore and the build descriptor from ProjectTemplates (Gradle application + mainClass, or a Maven POM whose compiler release comes from the selected JDK), downloads the chosen tool version through the Downloader/HttpDownloader seam and extracts it (Archives: pure-JDK extractZip/extractTarGz) into the project's own <root>/.espresso/tools/<tool>-<ver>/, then records the selection in <root>/.espresso/toolchain.properties (buildSystem, toolVersion, toolHome, jdkId). Compiling and running always resolve that project-local tool through ProjectToolchain (wrapper → .espresso/tools/… → a root-level distribution) and never fall back to the system gradle/mvn; a project with no provisioned tool gets a "not provisioned — no project Gradle/Maven" status answer that spawns nothing. Centrally, JDKs are *never* copied into a project: JdkRegistry indexes one shared store (~/.espresso/jdks/<version>/) plus user-registered folders (~/.espresso/jdks.properties), and a project only *selects* one by JdkEntry.id(), so two projects can target Java 25 and Java 21 without either carrying a private JDK, and JAVA_HOME is pinned to the selected JDK for every build/run (else the editor's own java.home). ManageJdksCard is the manager surface — its own in-panel card (no popups): a JList of JDKs, a version field + Download, *Register Existing Folder…*, Remove and Back — and ProjectCard links to it and lists JdkRegistry.list() (newest first) as the JDK selector. BuildSystem (GRADLE/MAVEN/NONE) carries each tool's wrapper name, launcher path, distribution prefix and download URL so provisioning and resolution share one source of truth; a plain-Java project (NONE) provisions no tool and compiles/runs with the selected JDK's own javac/java (JvmBuildTools resolves them from the project JDK first). Every download and extract is a seam, so 34 new headless cases prove the contract with no network: five new suites (ArchivesTest 4 — zip/tar.gz round-trip; JdkRegistryTest 7 — index the store + registered folders, resolve by id/version, persist, download via a fake Downloader landing in the store and never a project; ProjectProvisionerTest 6 — layout, toolchain.properties, per-BuildSystem descriptors, tool-less NONE, refuse-non-empty, unknown-JDK rejection before any write, and that no JDK is copied into the project; ProjectToolchainTest 7 — wrapper / .espresso/tools / root-level priority, no PATH, jdkHome via the registry; ManageJdksCardTest 3 — each button routes one host callback and the list reflects the registry) plus seven added to existing suites (ProjectCardTest NewProjectRequest assembly, two AdvancedTextEditorPanelTest provisioning cases driving provisionNewProject past the headless-unreachable chooser with an injected fake provisioner, and the hermetic launcher + JAVA_HOME-pinning cases in BuildToolsTest, GradleBuildToolsTest and MavenBuildToolsTest). Real network downloads cannot run in headless CI, so one end-to-end Gradle and one Maven provisioning are verified by hand and reported in the PR.
  • Mandela can now author a Presentoire deck — a shipped generator script and an Espresso starter template (lg3d-mandela, lg3d-apps, scripts) — The Markdown deck Presentoire opens is the one bridge between the two apps: lg3d-apps (Espresso) depends on lg3d-mandela but not on lg3d-incubator (Presentoire), and the language depends on nothing, so a deck capability in Mandela can only emit text. scripts/mandela/deck-new.mnd is a new generator beside userscript-new.mnd: run under a sandbox it writes a starter .md deck — a # title slide plus one slide per further argument, split on --- thematic breaks, with - bullets and plain paragraph lines, exactly the shape MarkdownDeckCodec reads back — and it refuses to overwrite a deck that already exists. Espresso reaches the same idea in-editor through a fourth EditorServices starter template, deck, surfaced by a fifth MandelaTools toolbar action, *Presentoire Deck* (mandela-deck, deliberately unbound like *Mandela Template*): it drops a console-safe program into an empty .mnd that assembles a small slide deck in a list and prints it, because Espresso runs the console profile with no filesystem, so writing the file stays the CLI script's job. Both are backward-compatible additions — no mandela.version or mandela.language bump and no desktop version change. 1 new headless case (MandelaToolsTest.deckTemplateNeedsWriteAndAnEmptyBuffer — the deck template goes into an empty buffer only with WRITE, prints to the Output panel without it, and never clobbers text), alongside the extended EditorServicesTest and MandelaToolsTest assertions and the new script compiled by ShippedScriptsTest. Presentoire needs no change: its Open action already sniffs a .md as a Markdown deck.
  • A bundled, full-featured Spring Boot web server that deploys and supervises containerized Spring Boot apps — the new lg3d-webserver module (lg3d-webserver) — The backend half of the todo.md *Webserver* item: a self-contained Spring Boot 3.5.6 (embedded Tomcat) server, built as an executable bootJar, exposing a management REST API that deploys and supervises containerized Spring Boot applications by shelling out to the system docker CLI (no docker-java, matching the desktop's Docker Manager), with a daemon-free local java -jar backend as its sibling. It follows the wonderland-server precedent exactly — the Spring Boot plugin, a bare library jar beside an -app-classified bootJar, and deliberately absent from the desktop classpath so Spring never enters the desktop JVM. Three layers keep it testable: config (WebServerProperties, @ConfigurationProperties("webserver")); deploy (the domain records Deployment/DeploymentRequest/AppState/DeploymentType/ CommandResult, the injectable seams ProcessLauncher + ChildProcessStarter + DockerCli, the DockerDeploymentBackend + JarProcessBackend, the Jackson DeploymentStore, and DeploymentRegistry — the orchestrator that allocates the id/name/context-path/host-port and reconciles recorded state against the live backend); and web (ServerManagementController, ReverseProxyFilter, ManagementAuthGate, ApiExceptionHandler). The API serves GET /api/server/{health,info,metrics}, GET/POST /api/apps, GET /api/apps/{id}, GET /api/apps/{id}/logs, POST /api/apps/{id}/{start,stop} and DELETE /api/apps/{id}, and reverse-proxies each running app under its own /{contextPath}/** on the server port. A Docker deploy is docker run -d --name <id> -p <port>:<port> -e SERVER_PORT=<port> …, so the host port, the published container port and the app's own server.port coincide and the container name is the stable deployment handle. The contract is never 500, never leak a stack trace: a missing daemon, a failed pull or an unbindable port becomes a readable DeploymentException the advice maps to 400/404/503, and with no daemon the server still boots and /api/server/health reports dockerAvailable=false. No credential is ever stored or logged (the management token is config-only, blank = open on loopback, compared in constant time), and deployment state persists as JSON under ~/.lg3d/webserver/deployments.json (overridable for test isolation). The module ships a multi-stage Dockerfile + docker-compose.yml, an application.properties documenting every knob with a bootRun --args example, and a role-aware AGENTS.md (indexed from the root guide). 136 new headless cases — @SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT) + MockMvc over every endpoint, a FakeDockerCli / fake ProcessLauncher proving the exact docker argv + stdout parsing and the no-daemon degradation, a fake ChildProcessStarter proving jar deploy/track/stop, the reverse proxy proved against an in-JVM com.sun.net.httpserver stub, and a @TempDir JSON round-trip — with a conservative lg3d-webserver coverage floor pinned in the root build.gradle and PIT report-only. Attributed to Jean-Francois Landreville in the file headers, the @author tags and the sign-off.
  • The Web Server Console — run and supervise that server and its deployed apps from inside the desktop (lg3d-apps, lg3d-core) — The frontend half: a new lg3d-apps start-menu app (org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.webserver, Developers group) that forks the lg3d-webserver bootJar as a child process (or attaches to one already running) and drives it over the management REST API with the JDK HttpClient + Jackson — the WonderlandWorldPanel / swing-ide precedent. lg3d-apps does not depend on lg3d-webserver: the console needs only the bootJar path (-Dwebserver.jar) to fork it and the server URL to talk to it, so Spring never enters the desktop JVM. WebServerConsole is the thin 3D entry point (a TitledSwingWindow hosting the panel on a SwingNode, 1024×768); WebServerConsolePanel is the main plain JPanel — a toolbar (Connect / Start local / Stop / Refresh), a status header and three tabs (Overview server info + JVM metrics, Applications a deployed-app table + an inline Deploy form + Start/Stop/Undeploy/Logs, Logs a tail) — with every HTTP/process call on a background executor landing back on the EDT and constructors that never throw; WebServerPanel is the 2D host shim the registry maps to. ManagementClient is the AWT-free REST client (an injectable Transport seam; a non-2xx becomes a ManagementException carrying the server's own {"error": …} sentence) and ServerProcessSupervisor forks java -jar <bootJar> --server.port=<p> behind an injectable Spawner, resolving the jar from -Dwebserver.jar → <lg.appcodebase>/libs/lg3d-webserver-*-app.jar → lg3d-webserver/build-gradle/libs/*-app.jar → “unavailable” (the panel degrades to a readable status line, never a throw or a modal). The dto/* records (HealthView, ServerInfoView, MetricsView, AppView, LogsView, DeployRequest) mirror the server's wire shape client-side so the console never imports a server class. lg3d-core wiring: Desktop2DAppRegistry maps the command to the hosted WebServerPanel (Kind.PANEL) for both desktops, a new webserver.png start-menu icon (drawn by lg3d-art's GenerateAppIcons), and :run / releaseBundle pass -Dwebserver.jar — the release bundle shipping the bootJar under server/ (not the lib/* desktop-classpath wildcard). 43 new headless cases (the panel's non-throwing construction + graceful degradation + dispose/refresh; ManagementClient against an in-JVM com.sun.net.httpserver fake; ServerProcessSupervisor jar-resolution + start/stop through a fake Spawner; dto round-trips) plus a Desktop2DAppRegistryTest.webServerConsoleIsHostedPanel mapping case. A new design note docs/webserver.md documents the two-process architecture. Live behaviour (connect, fork/stop a local child, deploy a containerized app) needs a running server, so it is verified with the in-JVM probe + internal screencapture rather than asserted here.
  • Presentoire now reads and writes Markdown decks — open a .md (or a set of them) and Save As .md, in pure Java (lg3d-incubator, lg3d-apps) — A fifth format joins the presentoire.format layer with no new dependency: MarkdownDeckCodec is a line scanner over the same AWT-free PresentoireModel the other codecs hand both renderers. Import splits a single .md into slides on the boundaries the popular slide dialects share — a thematic break (---, and the CommonMark ***/___ forms) and a top-level # heading — or, through DeckCodecs.openMarkdown, turns a chosen set of .md files into one slide each, ordered by name. Within a slide the first # heading is the title, ## ..###### are sub-headings, a run of plain lines is a paragraph, -/*/+/1. items are a bullet list, and a line holding only an embedded image (its alt text and a file path) is a picture read from disk beside the .md into the model's in-memory image map (a missing or remote image is skipped, never fetched, never fatal); inline markup (bold, italics, code spans and links) is flattened to plain text. Because Markdown carries no page geometry, the codec lays each slide out itself — a top-down vertical flow in the document's -0.1..0.1 slide units, word-wrapped to a column budget and uniformly scaled to fit — honouring SlideRenderer's bottom-left (text/list) and centre (image) anchoring, so an imported deck renders where the built-in one does. Export (the 2D panel's Save As…) writes slides separated by ---, a slide's first text block as its # title, sub-headed text as ## , list items as - bullets, and every picture once into a sibling <name>.assets/ folder referenced by relative path, so a deck round-trips (colours do not survive — Markdown has none; text, structure and pictures do). DeckCodecs sniffs .md/.markdown by extension (plain text has no magic bytes), and the panel's Open and Save As filters gained both with multi-select enabled, so several .md files open as one deck. Fidelity is bounded as for the office codecs: tables, reference-style links/images, nested lists (flattened to one level), an image embedded mid-paragraph (reduced to its alt text) and syntax highlighting are dropped. 23 new headless cases — a new MarkdownDeckCodecTest (17 — split on ---/headings, chunk→elements, inline flattening, pictures from disk, the fit-to-slide layout, multi-file readAll, the export structure and .assets/ siblings, and the round trip), plus DeckCodecsTest (9→12 — the .md-by-extension sniff, formatFor/fromExtension for .md/.markdown, and openMarkdown routing with its non-Markdown rejection) and PresentoirePanelTest (11→14 — the multi-file openFiles deck, its null/empty/non-Markdown rejection, and saveFile MARKDOWN). The 3D face is unchanged (it renders the very same model), so no desktop launch is required.
  • Presentoire now speaks PowerPoint and LibreOffice — open *and* save .pptx, legacy .ppt and .odp, plus a bundled Looking Glass deck (lg3d-incubator, lg3d-apps, lg3d-core) — Presentoire read only its own native .zip and opened on a three-slide placeholder. A new AWT-free presentoire.format layer round-trips four formats through the one shared PresentoireModel, so the 3D Frame3D and the 2D PresentoirePanel render an imported deck identically. DeckCodecs.open sniffs the format by magic bytes, not extension (OLE2 → .ppt; ZIP → read the archive: ppt/presentation.xml → .pptx, a leading mimetype of application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.presentation → .odp, else a <document> root → native .zip; falling back to the extension), and DeckCodecs.export writes any of the four. .pptx (XSLF) and the legacy binary .ppt (HSLF) go through Apache POI — the module's one new dependency (poi-ooxml + poi-scratchpad, re-resolved onto the :lg3d-core:run / releaseBundle classpath as presentoireLibs); .odp (OpenDocument) and the native .zip stay pure-Java ZIP+DOM, and the native format gains the writer it never had. SlideGeometry maps an office page (4:3 / 16:9) onto Presentoire's square -0.1..0.1 slide fit-inside, aspect-preserving and centred — text/lists bottom-left anchored, images centre anchored, mirroring SlideRenderer so an import→export round trip lands where the renderer already draws. Fidelity is deliberately bounded to the Presentoire vocabulary (text blocks, bullet lists, pictures): themes, custom fonts, animations, tables, charts and grouped/rotated shapes are dropped on import and never emitted on export. PresentoireModel generalised to carry images in memory (of(...) + an inlineImages map) so a deck is no longer tied to an on-disk ZipFile, and ModelColor.toHex feeds the writers' solid fills. The 2D panel gains a Save As… button and a multi-format file filter and names the detected source format on its status line; the 3D viewer stays read-only. Both faces now open by default on a complete 16-slide *Looking Glass 3D and 2D* presentation (LOOKING_GLASS_XML, text/vector-only — a compiled-in constant, no binary/LFS) covering the 3D scene-graph desktop, the 2D/Swing MDI desktop, the shared-model pattern, the apps portfolio, Project Mandela, the build toolchain and Presentoire's own format support, with the port attributed to Jean-Francois Landreville. 37 new headless cases — 32 in the new presentoire.format suite (DeckCodecsTest 9 on magic-byte sniffing + routing, NativeDeckCodecTest 6, PptxDeckCodecTest 3, PptDeckCodecTest 3, OdpDeckCodecTest 4 including the mimetype-first- uncompressed ODF rule, SlideGeometryTest 7 on the fit-inside inverse transform) plus 5 added to PresentoireModelTest (11→14) and PresentoirePanelTest (9→11) for the default deck, of(...) inline images, toHex, per-format open and saveFile export. The 3D scene-graph view needs a live display, so it is verified with the in-JVM probe and internal screencapture rather than asserted here.
  • Presentoire is resurrected — the 2006 slide-deck viewer ported to JDK 21 and wired into both desktops (lg3d-incubator, lg3d-apps, lg3d-core) — Presentoire compiled but was a dormant prototype: its start-menu descriptor sat in the incubator's own unscanned src/config, and — fatally on a modern JVM — PresentoireDocument built a JavaScript ScriptEngine *while parsing*, so any deck carrying a language="JavaScript" transition threw a RuntimeException before a single slide appeared (Nashorn was removed in JDK 15), and its document picker was a "MUST DISAPPEAR AS SOON AS POSSIBLE" modal JDialog with a hardcoded /home/debian/... path. It now runs on both desktops from one AWT-free model. presentoire.model (PresentoireModel, SlideModel, SlideElement, ModelColor, ScriptTransitionModel) is the single parser both faces read: it turns a deck ZIP (content.xml plus the images it names) into an immutable slide tree, hardens the XML reader against entity expansion, fixes the original's /254 colour drift to /255, and parses a <transition> to inert data so the JavaScript case no longer throws — the 3D ScriptTransition degrades to a plain slide swap when no engine is present. The native-3D Presentoire / PresentoireDocument / Slide / elements / transition classes were refactored onto that model (renderers never return null; the debug println/printStackTrace spam and the raw Vector/Class are gone, and the private-runTransition base swap the 2006 code actually relied on is preserved rather than activating unverified scene-graph animation). The 2D/Swing desktop gets a new idiomatic document viewer, PresentoirePanel — a toolbar (open, first/prev/slide n of N/ next/last, zoom out/percent/zoom in/fit width), a scrollable canvas that centres the slide, and a status line — which SlideRenderer rasterises with Java 2D from the very same SlideModel the 3D face builds Component3D nodes from, so the two desktops can never disagree about a deck and the panel loads no Java 3D. Both faces open on a built-in three-slide demo deck (no binary blob, no hardcoded path) and load a real deck through a standard JFileChooser; the modal FileChooser hack is deleted. Per the hosted-panel palette rule the panel chrome wears only LAF colours — the sole painted pixels are inside the rendered slide bitmap, which is document content (a white page and the deck's own ink), exactly as a PDF page is. It is registered in Desktop2DAppRegistry.PANEL_APPS against the 3D main class, and one shared descriptor lg3d-apps/src/config/presentoire.lgcfg (Office group, the app's own bundled presentoire.png icon resolved from the incubator jar) launches the Frame3D in the 3D desktop and the panel as an MDI frame in the 2D desktop. The port and its subsequent modifications are attributed to Jean-Francois Landreville in the file headers, the @author tags, the commit sign-off and a new AboutInfo.PORTED_APPLICATIONS line the About box renders on both desktops. 20 new headless cases (PresentoireModelTest 11 on the pure parser, the ModelColor /255 fix, the JavaScript-transition no-throw fix, XXE rejection and a real-ZIP image round-trip; PresentoirePanelTest 9 on the SlideRenderer white-page/ink raster and the panel's navigation/zoom clamps and open/reject flow), plus a Desktop2DAppRegistryTest.presentoireIsHostedPanel mapping case. The 3D scene-graph view needs a live display, so it is verified with the in-JVM probe and internal screencapture rather than asserted here.
  • Physics is resurrected — the 2006 rigid-body playground ported to JDK 21 and wired into both desktops as a Newton's cradle (lg3d-incubator, lg3d-apps, lg3d-core) — The Physics app compiled but was a dormant prototype: its start-menu descriptor sat in the incubator's own unscanned src/config (naming a physics.jar and a PhysTest class that no longer exist), its engine inventory carried a one-byte empty RigidBodyState stub, and — the blocker for the 2D/Swing desktop — PhysicsObject imports org.jogamp.java3d.* and Component3D at class level, so reusing the engine would drag the scene graph into a desktop that must never load it. The resurrection leaves the working native-3D engine and its demos (NewtonCradleDemo, PhysicsTutorial1/2) exactly as they are — they already build on the Jogamp Java 3D and carry their @author Tobias Evert tags — and adds the one thing they lacked: an AWT-free, Java 3D-free planar core, physics.model (Vec2, Particle, Spring, NewtonCradleModel), that reproduces the demo's dynamics with the same algorithm and the same physical constants (seven 1.1 kg balls at restitution 0.95, g 5.81, damped strings at k 205.9 / damping 206.2) over a leapfrog integrator, an iterated Newton-Coulomb impulse resolver and a mass-weighted positional-correction pass — the PhysicsThread.run() sequence reduced to synchronous planar form. On it the 2D/Swing desktop gets NewtonCradlePanel, a desk-toy viewer that paints the cradle (support bar, strings, radial-gradient steel balls) with Java 2D into a canvas fit to the model's static world bounds, runs on a javax.swing.Timer started in addNotify and stopped in removeNotify (so closing the window never leaks a timer and a headless host never spawns one), and re-pulls the first ball on a fixed cadence once the impacts have bled the motion into a gentle common-mode sway. Both desktops therefore swing the same cradle with the same physics; only the renderer differs. It is registered in Desktop2DAppRegistry.PANEL_APPS against the NewtonCradleDemo main class, and one shared descriptor lg3d-apps/src/config/newtonscradle.lgcfg (Education group, a generated newtonscradle.png glass tile from lg3d-art/tools/GenerateAppIcons.java) launches the Frame3D in the 3D desktop and the panel as an MDI frame in the 2D desktop. The empty RigidBodyState stub is deleted. Per the hosted-panel palette rule the toolbar, buttons and status line wear only LAF colours — the sole painted pixels are the rendered simulation content, exactly as ChessPanel's board is. The port and its subsequent modifications are attributed to Jean-Francois Landreville in the file headers (every physics source now carries the Sun + Portions banner, the original @author tags preserved), the commit sign-off and the AboutInfo.PORTED_APPLICATIONS line, which now names Physics beside Presentoire. 21 new headless cases (NewtonCradleModelTest 14 on the Vec2/Particle/ Spring primitives and the simulation — the release pose, one-ball-in-one-ball-out momentum transfer through a resting chain whose middle balls stay put, energy decay, balls never leaving the world bounds nor visibly interpenetrating, the step clamp and reset, and determinism; NewtonCradlePanelTest 7 on the headless build, the start/pause/toggle flags, the one-fixed-frame tick, the restart cadence, reset, the status line and a non-blank canvas raster), plus a Desktop2DAppRegistryTest.newtonCradleIsHostedPanel mapping case. The 3D scene-graph view needs a live display, so it is verified by compile and code review rather than asserted here.
  • Screen Snapshot now chooses *what* to grab — whole screen, every window, or a region you drag out (lg3d-apps, lg3d-core) — The Screen Snapshot utility captured exactly one thing before: whatever the desktop's own capture path produced after a delay. It now asks the user to pick a CaptureArea — Whole screen, All windows or A region I select — as three radio buttons in the config frame, and honours that choice on both desktops. The 2D/Swing desktop has no scene graph to read a raster from and java.awt.Robot cannot grab a rootless/Wayland display, so DesktopScreenshot renders the desktop straight into images by painting its own Swing windows offscreen: captureFullScreen composites every visible top-level window into one screen-sized PNG (MDI desktop-root frames painted first so conventional app windows land on top), captureAllWindows writes each window to its own PNG (the JDesktopPane's visible internal frames, plus any conventional top-level window), and captureRegion composites then crops to the selection. The 3D desktop keeps its event seam: FULL_SCREEN and ALL_WINDOWS both post a whole-canvas ScreenCaptureEvent (the scene graph already renders every window into one canvas), and SELECTION posts the same event carrying a crop Rectangle, which ScreenCaptureBehavior now applies to the raster it reads back via the new pure RasterCrop before writing the file. RegionSelector is the drag-select overlay: a full-screen JWindow (never a Frame, so it is excluded from the composite and disposed before the capture runs — it can never appear in its own snapshot) that punches the selection clear with per-pixel translucency where supported, falls back to a uniform 0.45 window opacity, then to an opaque veil with instructions; Escape or a sub-4px drag cancels. The selection rectangle, the window-bounds union, the clamp-to-screen and the crop are all pure arithmetic in CaptureRegions (2D) and RasterCrop (3D); file naming stays lgscreen-<index>-<n>.png, so a 2D and a 3D snapshot are indistinguishable in ~/Documents/Screenshots. ScreenCaptureEvent gained an optional, defensively-copied region (setRegion/getRegion/hasRegion) that defaults to null — a whole-canvas capture — so every existing caller is untouched. 30 new headless cases (CaptureAreaTest 3 on the labels; CaptureRegionsTest 8 on normalise/union/clamp/crop including the disjoint and null rejections; ScreenshotFilesTest 5 on the naming, default directory and writer; DesktopScreenshotTest 5 on the desktop-pane search, the visible-internal-frame filter and the headless empty-bounds fallback; RasterCropTest 4 on the 3D crop's pixels/clamp/reject; ScreenCaptureEventTest 5 on the region round-trip, defensive copy and null-clear). The paint calls, the read-back raster and the live overlay need a display, so the on-screen result is verified by launching the desktop and checking the produced lgscreen-*.png — not asserted here. Known limitation: external native (non-Java) application windows cannot be enumerated without Robot, so "All windows" covers the desktop's own Swing/3D windows, not foreign X11 clients composited alongside.
  • Contact darkening now ships on the live canvas — roadmap P2.7, screen-space ambient occlusion on the post chain (wonderland-renderer) — The fifth and final link on the preSwap GPU post chain the P3.2 bloom proved, run FIRST so the scene is occluded before the cosmetic lens effects and the tone map fold it — same shipped pattern as the bloom, tone map, FXAA and DOF: a pure headless-tested kernel, a probe-gated GL pass transcribing it, a plan decision, an opt-in flag and the WorldViewer wiring, with the depth buffer the defocus introduced now put to reconstructing a normal. SsaoKernel is the occlusion estimate in pure Java: the symmetric-perspective unprojection (near*far/(far - d*(far-near))), a view normal from the reconstructed position's screen-space gradients flipped toward the eye, and a fixed twelve-point hemisphere sampled with a deterministic per-pixel rotation, a depth range-check and a self-bias, counting how many samples a nearer surface hides; it reuses HdrKernel.Frame, and apply() modulates the composited RGB — the honest approximation available to a pass that sees the final frame and not the direct/ambient split. GpuSsaoPass blits FB0 colour+depth into scene textures, runs the hemisphere sample and multiplies back into the swap buffer with zero CPU readback and the same GL state bracket and never-throws latch; SSAO_FRAG is SsaoKernel transcribed with the identical twelve sample literals, the identical integer per-pixel rotation and a texelFetch for every depth read so a sample lands on the exact texel the kernel indexes. PostProcessPlan.decideSsao answers the GPU route or NONE, never a half-applied software darkening that would leave the live canvas flat-lit. WorldViewer prepends the pass, built with the camera-matched Settings it derives from the scene's own near/far/fov and the canvas aspect (front clip extracted to FRONT_CLIP_M so the reconstruction cannot drift from the view show() sets). 20 new headless cases (SsaoKernelTest 11 — the linearisation spans near..far and is monotonic, a flat field is unoccluded everywhere, a pit floor beside its wall is occluded but its flat middle is not, a raised platform is not, the factor stays in 0..1, a zero intensity is the exact identity and a far-clip background is untouched; GpuSsaoPassTest 5 on the settings contract and the null-context render/dispose no-op guards; the four decideSsao branches in PostProcessPlanTest). The GL pass cannot be constructed headless (a GLContext needs a display), so the on-screen darkening is verified by the in-JVM probe under DISPLAY, exactly like the bloom — not asserted here.
  • The frame now defocuses by depth — roadmap P3.5, depth of field on the post chain (wonderland-renderer) — The fourth link on the preSwap GPU post chain, after the tone map and before FXAA so the defocus gathers the display-referred image and the anti-alias still runs last — same shipped pattern as the bloom, tone map and FXAA, with the one thing that sets this link apart: a depth buffer. DofKernel is the scatter-as-gather defocus in pure Java — the circle of confusion a normalised depth implies (clamp01 of the depth error over the focus band, symmetric about the focus), the round(coc * maxRadiusPx) gather radius, and a disc average that skips an out-of-frame or outside-the-disc sample and divides by the count it kept — reusing HdrKernel.Frame so the chain agrees on one frame type. GpuDofPass is the first pass to blit DEPTH beside colour (GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT, GL_NEAREST as a depth blit requires) into a paired GL_DEPTH_COMPONENT24 attachment, because at preSwap the depth the renderer just wrote is still resident on the GPU; DOF_FRAG is DofKernel.gather transcribed, the only divergence being the sub-LSB fixed-point rounding every pass in this chain has. PostProcessPlan.decideDof answers the GPU route or NONE, never a half-applied software defocus that would leave the live canvas uniformly sharp. WorldViewer inserts the pass between the tone map and FXAA and adds getDofDecision(); the scene depth survives bloom and the tone map (both write only colour), so DOF reads the true depth wherever it sits. 19 new headless cases (DofKernelTest 10 — the CoC is 0 at the focus, monotonic, symmetric and saturating, the radius caps, a zero max radius is the exact identity, a uniform frame survives ANY depth field untouched (the invariant that proves the gather invents no detail), and a focus pixel stays sharp while a far pixel blurs; GpuDofPassTest 5; the four decideDof branches in PostProcessPlanTest). The GL pass is probe-gated like every link on this chain.
  • Physically-based shading has a kernel and a plan now — roadmap P2.6, Cook-Torrance metallic-roughness BRDF (wonderland-renderer) — A metallic-roughness BRDF the lit route can run instead of Blinn-Phong, delivered in the exact shape P2.2's ShaderAppearancePlan shipped. PbrKernel (in shade) is Cook-Torrance in pure Java — GGX/Trowbridge-Reitz normal distribution D, Smith-Schlick geometry G, Schlick Fresnel F, the dielectric-0.04 / metal-base-colour F0, and the assembled energy-conserving direct-light BRDF plus a shade() that adds ambient, java.base only. PbrPlan (in mesh) is the headless verdict of "does this material run Cook-Torrance", with a reason beside every branch, carrying the GLSL 1.20 vertex+fragment pair that transcribes PbrKernel (same PI, same 0.04 F0, same D/G/F, same alpha = roughness^2). It is probe-gated exactly like P2.2's SHADER path: production keeps the validated Blinn-Phong route until a WlProbe validates this program, and a material falls back with its metallic/roughness recorded but unapplied rather than silently flat — so no shipped world changes a pixel yet. 17 new headless cases (PbrKernelTest 10 pin the physical invariants — dielectric F0 0.04, a metal's F0 is its base, Fresnel head-on vs grazing, GGX sharpens as roughness falls, Smith in (0,1], BRDF non-negative and zero below the horizon, a black metal reflects nothing, shade scales by the cosine; PbrPlanTest 7 pin every decision branch and that the GLSL names the kernel's constants). The live route is probe-gated, not asserted, exactly like P2.2.
  • The presented image now anti-aliases — roadmap P3.4, FXAA subpixel pass on the post chain (wonderland-renderer) — The third link on the preSwap GPU post chain, after the bloom and the tone map so it softens the edges of the very image the eye is shown — same shipped pattern: a pure headless-tested kernel, a probe-gated GL pass transcribing it, a plan decision, an opt-in flag and the WorldViewer wiring. FxaaKernel is FXAA's published subpixel stage — the local-contrast edge gate plus the subpixel blend toward the four-neighbour average, using Lottes's FXAA_SUBPIX_TRIM 1/4 and its 1/(1-trim) scale, clamped by the subpixel quality — reusing HdrKernel's luminance and Frame so the whole chain agrees on one definition of "how bright". It is the subpixel stage only, not FXAA's directional span search, and claims no more. GpuFxaaPass captures FB0 into a scene texture, runs a fullscreen subpixel pass and writes back into the swap buffer, zero readback, same GL state bracket and never-throws latch; FXAA_FRAG is FxaaKernel transcribed. PostProcessPlan.decideFxaa answers the GPU route or NONE, never a half-applied software anti-alias that would leave the live canvas jagged. WorldViewer appends the pass last and adds getFxaaDecision(). 18 new headless cases (FxaaKernelTest 9 — a flat frame is byte-for-byte unchanged, the gate needs both floor and luma fraction, an isolated impulse is pulled toward its average by exactly the published weight and nothing else in the field moves, alpha carried through; GpuFxaaPassTest 5; the four decideFxaa branches in PostProcessPlanTest). Probe-gated GL pass.
  • The live canvas now tone maps — roadmap P3.3, HDR on the post chain (wonderland-renderer, wonderland-common) — The second link on the preSwap GPU post chain the P3.2 bloom proved, following the shipped pattern exactly: a pure headless-tested kernel, a probe-gated GL pass, a plan decision, an opt-in feature flag and the WorldViewer wiring. HdrKernel is the pure tone-mapping reference — exposure, extended Reinhard with a white point, Narkowicz ACES, Rec.709 luminance and gamma encode — over a packed ARGB int[] and float triples, java.base only. GpuPostEffect is the one contract every GPU pass now honours (render/dispose/isFailed); GpuBloomPass declares it unchanged. GpuHdrPass captures FB0 into a scene texture, runs a fullscreen tonemap and writes back into the swap buffer, zero CPU readback, same GL state bracket and never-throws latch as the bloom; its GLSL is HdrKernel.curve transcribed. PostProcessCanvas generalizes the old single-pass BloomCanvas into an ordered GpuPostEffect chain that skips any failed link inside one preSwap (BloomCanvas removed). PostProcessPlan.decideHdr answers the GPU route or NONE, never a half-applied software curve that would leave the live canvas lying about its own radiance. WorldFeatures gained the HDR/FXAA/DOF/SSAO/PBR flags (ON by default like every switch there), and WorldViewer builds the chain from both decisions and adds getHdrDecision(). 21 new headless cases (HdrKernelTest 12; GpuHdrPassTest 5; the four decideHdr branches in PostProcessPlanTest), and the WorldFeatures summary now names every flag. The on-screen GL pass is probe-gated like the bloom.
  • A live per-frame GPU bloom now ships — roadmap P3.2, the ceiling retired by patching the renderer (wonderland-renderer, wonderland-common) — The earlier P3.2 entries in this section bloomed a *captured* frame in software and stated, honestly for their moment, that a per-frame glow on the LIVE 3D canvas was "a missing architecture, not a missing flag" because the fork had no scene-to-texture path a shader could sample. That claim is now retired, not softened. WlProbe53 first re-measured the ceiling and found it lower than the prose assumed: a framebuffer blit of the presented scene into a texture and back (FBO-BLIT-OK) runs on the live GL 4.6 radeonsi context at 56 fps, and an inline bright-pass/blur/composite lifted a hot quad's halo — so a GPU post pass is real-time on this fork and the renderer is hookable. The hook did not exist upstream: Java 3D 1.7.2 offers postRender, but WlProbe54 proved it UNVIABLE (FB0 reads black there — it fires before the sync render — and it cost ~1 s/frame). So the renderer is patched: lg3d-core/src/patches/java3d-core-preswap adds an overridable public Canvas3D.preSwap() (no-op base) that Renderer calls between its syncRender glFinish and swapBuffers, guarded against a RuntimeException/Error so an app hook can never take the render thread down. The patch is built from source in CI, never committed as a binary: :buildPatchedJava3dCore clones upstream java3d-core 1.7.2 at a pinned SHA, applies the committed .patch, Maven-builds it under JDK 21 and installs it into a local repo declared *before* Maven Central under the *same* coordinates, so the patched jar shadows stock for every consumer (PROVENANCE.txt + the upstream license travel with it). On that hook GpuBloomPass runs the production zero-readback GL chain — blit FB0 into a scene texture, smooth-kneed bright pass, separable 9-tap Gaussian ping-pong, additive composite — with the whole GL state (draw/read FBO, viewport, program, VAO, active texture, unit 0/1 bindings and the blend/depth/scissor/cull enables) saved and restored around it, because leaking Java 3D's state is what turned the next frame black. It never throws: any GL fault latches the pass off and the desktop renders clean. BloomCanvas is the thin preSwap adapter that drives it, and WorldViewer builds one only when PostProcessPlan.decide(...) answers the new GPU_POSTPROCESS path — gated on WorldFeatures.BLOOM (lg.wonderland.bloom=off disables it) AND a runtime check that the patched hook is actually present, so an unpatched jar silently keeps the plain Canvas3D. PostProcessPlan gained Path.GPU_POSTPROCESS and Capability.GPU_POSTPROCESS_PROBED_USABLE, checked *before* the readback route so the zero-readback path always wins when both are in evidence. WlProbe55 measured an inline chain VISIBLE per frame at 71 fps (7732 halo pixels lifted onto dark scene); WlProbe56 re-measured the PRODUCTION GpuBloomPass at PROD-BLOOM-VISIBLE, 94 fps (10.67 ms mean / 11.54 ms max at 1280x763), the before/after FB0 diff lifting the same 7732 pixels, every one onto dark background (the halo a viewer actually sees), max lift 75, prodPassFailed=false — the shipped uniform-parameterised chain reproduces the proven constants exactly. The GL chain and BloomCanvas cannot be constructed headless (a GLContext needs a display), so they are probe-verified; the pure halves are asserted — 15 new headless cases (PostProcessPlanTest 8 on the full decision matrix including the GPU branch and its preference over readback; GpuBloomPassTest 7 on the Settings defaults being the exact proved constants, negative-magnitude refusal, and the null-context render/dispose no-op guards), plus WorldFeatures.BLOOM in WorldFeaturesTest. No shipped world changes a pixel until a host opts into bloom AND runs on the patched jar.
  • A captured frame can bloom now — roadmap P3.2, the software-capture pass wired and measured (wonderland-renderer) — BloomKernel had shipped the three operations every bloom is (smooth-kneed bright pass, separable clamped box blur, saturating add) as pure arithmetic on packed ARGB pixels, and PostProcessPlan the checked decision about where a bloom may run, but nothing called either: the software-capture route the plan named "always available" was prose, and the live OFFSCREEN_READBACK route was gated on a readback measurement nobody had taken. BloomPass is the seam that makes the software route real — hand it the frame a readRaster or a 2D composite produced plus what the host knows, and it consults the plan and returns what it allows: the exact identity (the same object, not a copy) for NONE, so a world that never asked for a glow is untouched by the pass being wired, and the bloomed frame otherwise, bridging a BufferedImage to the kernel and back. WlProbe52 then took the measurement the live route waits on, on the repo's own X:0 / GL 4.6 radeonsi display: it ran the fork's readback round trip — capture the live canvas, convert to packed ARGB, bloom it through the wired BloomPass — and timed it at ~128 ms for a 640x363 frame and ~419 ms for a native 1920x1080 software bloom. It proved the bloom correct on a LIVE capture, not just a synthetic array: the halo around a hot white quad lifted from luminance 69 to 76, lit pixels grew 50,176 → 54,644, total luminance rose by 151,336, and the wired BloomPass produced byte-identical pixels to the raw BloomKernel. So the round trip WORKS — a software-capture bloom is real and now has a caller — but it costs far more than a real-time frame at native resolution, which is the honest reason PostProcessPlan keeps the per-frame OFFSCREEN_READBACK route gated behind READBACK_PROBED_USABLE (its reason now cites the measured number rather than "no measurement exists yet") and the shipping default stays SOFTWARE_CAPTURE: stills, on-demand snapshots, probe captures and 2D composites. 11 new headless cases (BloomPassTest): the default settings are the ones the probe measured, every negative magnitude is refused, NONE and a null decision are the pixel-perfect identity (same object back), a null frame or image is returned null rather than invented, a bloom path glows a hot spot's dark neighbour, OFFSCREEN_READBACK blooms identically to SOFTWARE_CAPTURE, the capability overload decides-then-applies, null settings fall back to the default, the BufferedImage seam carries alpha and round-trips pixels exactly, and the plan's reason now cites the measurement. No shipped world changes a pixel: nothing asks for bloom, so the pass is the identity until a host opts in.
  • A glossy surface now reflects the sky — roadmap P2.5, environment cube map wired and measured (wonderland-renderer) — EnvMapKernel, EnvironmentPlan and CubeMapArt had shipped the maths, the decision and a procedural six-face gradient, but nothing bound a cube map to a live program: the environment fragment declared its eye and normal vectors as UNIFORMS (one reflection direction for the whole surface, so it would read flat), had no vertex stage to link against, and read gl_FragColor before writing it — undefined. Two probes on the repo's live X:0 / GL 4.6 radeonsi context settled the one unknown the route rested on and then drove the shipping path. WlProbe50 proved a samplerCube binds its own texture unit and samples the correct face on this Jogamp fork — three quads each sampling one hardcoded direction read +X red, +Y green, +Z blue back — once the faces go on with the fork's TextureCubeMap.setImage(LEVEL, FACE, image) argument order: the first index is the mip level (checkImageSize shifts the expected image size by it), the second the face 0..5, so passing a face constant first reads it as a level and throws "illegal image size" — the same class of binding omission that once mis-read the fork as single-texture. EnvironmentPlan now carries a complete GLSL 1.20 pair: ENV_VERTEX_GLSL writes the eye-space vEyeNormal/vViewDir varyings P2.2 already proved live, and ENV_FRAGMENT_GLSL samples the diffuse, lights it, then lays reflect/refract cube lookups weighted by Schlick fresnel over that lit base at the material's reflectivity — EnvMapKernel.composite spelled in shading language, so the headless kernel and the program cannot disagree. J3dMeshFactory.buildEnvAppearance binds it: the lit diffuse on unit 0, the shared procedural TextureCubeMap (built from CubeMapArt.gradientFaces(), each face's pixels painted before attach) on unit 1, both samplers named and assigned their unit. WlProbe51 drove the SHIPPING createShape and read a lit red diffuse quad at (255,0,0) become (230,97,110) once an environment cube was attached at half reflectivity — still red-dominant (the diffuse bound) with its green and blue lifted by the sampled sky gradient (the cube bound beside it); an unbound cube samples black and would have left green and blue at zero, so the tint is the proof. The route is opt-in behind the same triply-conservative gate as P2.2 (lg.wonderland.shader, lit(), a resolved diffuse) plus EnvironmentPlan.decide(...).appliesEnvironment(), so a material that names no cube map keeps the plain Blinn-Phong program and a pre-P2.5 world changes not a pixel. 3 new headless cases (EnvironmentPlanTest): the fragment reads per-vertex varyings not one uniform eye vector, it blends the environment over a sampled diffuse base with exactly one gl_FragColor write, and the vertex stage writes the varyings the fragment consumes.
  • The environment has a source now — roadmap P2.5, default cube map (wonderland-renderer) — EnvMapKernel and EnvironmentPlan had shipped the maths and the decision for reflection/refraction, but the first glossy material had no image to sample: no shipped COLLADA world names a reflection map (the 2006 <reflectivity> channel is read by TextureBindingPlan yet its texture reference never resolves), so the plan could only ever answer FIXED with the lost effects named. CubeMapArt is the missing source — a procedural six-face environment gradient (64 px per face, power-of-two, POS_Y zenith / NEG_Y nadir / four side faces ramping sky→horizon→ground), rasterised headless in pure java2d so the layout and the PNG round trip are CI-asserted, while wrapping the faces into a live TextureCubeMap and binding it to a ShaderAppearance stays the fork's probe-side half (Java 3D needs a GL context), exactly as P2.2/P3.2 left theirs. 9 new headless cases (CubeMapArtTest): the face packing and power-of-two size, every pixel opaque, the two caps solid, the side ramp's exact endpoints and its horizon-band middle, one row flat across, all four sides agreeing on the ramp, and a face encoding to a PNG that reads back identical pixels (an out-of-range index yields none). No shipped world changes a pixel: a plain material names no cube map and ior == 1, so EnvironmentPlan still answers FIXED.
  • The pond is no longer just a record — roadmap P2.3, wired (wonderland-renderer) — WaterInstance and WaterArt shipped as a parsed record and a headless-rasterised seamless tile that nothing placed in the scene graph: the data survived the read and the look existed only as arithmetic. WorldScene.collectWater is the new decision layer — it gates on WorldFeatures.WATER, folds each record's plane through WaterArt.planeOf, and refuses a degenerate extent (the same guard that keeps a bad .dep from taking a world down) so a zero-area water record is one fewer pond rather than a NaN the traverser has to carry. WorldScene.addWater is the scene-graph half: one flatQuad per pond, sized by the record's own half-extents, seated by pondSeat — the cell's composed matrix outside and the record's translation and optional AxisAngle4d rotation inside, the same order every other placement here uses; a zero-length axis is refused rather than fed to AxisAngle4d, so an author who wrote an angle with no axis gets the plane they did not ask to turn. Each pond hangs behind its own Switch gate named after the cell that carries it, so cullTo shuts the water with the ground under it (pondsHiddenLastFrame is the count the probe reads beside pondCount). A TexCoordGeneration (OBJECT_LINEAR, TEXTURE_COORDINATE_2, ALLOW_PLANE_WRITE) sits on each quad's Appearance so WaterArt.TILE_UNITS tiles the plane's own space — a 100-unit pond gets 25 ripples whatever scale the deployment put it at — and WorldArt.planeS/planeT are the four-number planes the frame clock writes, the S offset riding in the constant component so the tile size never moves with the clock.
