The world is now tiled outward from the hall, every shared boundary coincident by construction: the lobby keeps x −11..+11, z −8..+8; row A (z −14..−8) holds four 5.5 m bays — Exam Room 1, Exam Room 2, Patient Education, Observation Room — and row B (z −20..−14) holds the two 11 m anterooms behind them, so each waiting room abuts the exam room it serves. The waiting rooms are raised from 1.2 m to the same 3.4 m ceiling as the rest, and the floor is cut to the building's footprint plus 20 cm: a floor bigger than the building standing on it is the single clearest tell that the rooms were placed rather than built. Each room cube is drawn 5 cm smaller than its bay on every axis, because two coplanar surfaces of one colour are a z-fight and a seam you can see through is cheaper than a shimmer you cannot stop. Proven with the in-JVM probe: a plan-view frame from above the roof reads one contiguous footprint (74 distinct colours in the frame, against the single flat colour a failed frame returns), and a frame from the middle of Exam Room 1 shows a room with a ceiling over it rather than a shell on a plain. What this does not yet claim is a doorway cut into the shared wall — the rooms are shells, and the walk has no collision to open a door against, so entering one still means walking through plaster.
  • The lg3d-core coverage floor is raised to 0.225 line / 0.310 branch (build.gradle) — it sat at 0.010 / 0.020, a floor written when the module had two small suites. The measured numbers are now 22.83% / 31.56%, and org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.crash alone is at 92.43% line / 82.16% branch; the rest of the gap is the 2006-era scene graph, which needs a live 3D desktop and is verified with the in-JVM probe instead (see AGENTS.md). A regression of the crash pipeline now fails check rather than quietly reopening the gap.
  • The language guide now says what the machine does (docs/mandela-language.md) — three sentences were wrong, and each is the kind an author repeats without checking. *Truthiness*: the guide said only false and null are false, while the engine also calls 0, 0.0 and "" false and an empty [], {} and 1..0 true. *Iteration*: the guide listed the pair spellings but never said that a single name binds the value — so a map loop hands out values, not keys — nor which six shapes may be walked, that null is the empty sequence, or that the loop reads the live container. *Operators*: the guide now states the == rules the engine applies (numbers across kinds, contents all the way down for a List, a Map and a type, identity for a class and an enum constant), the as Any identity conversion, and that a downward inclusive range reaches its end.
  • The values package is at every line covered (lg3d-mandela) — ValuesTest, IterationTest (the for cursor and range counting) and ValueTypesTest (the Java surface a host and the machine share: what a Callable reports about itself, a class about its constructor, a wrapped host exception, and where a container says no) join the suite: 1142 headless cases, 89.3% line coverage for the module, and org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values at 809 of 809 lines.
  • The lg3d-mandela coverage floor is raised to 0.890 line / 0.780 branch (build.gradle) — the ratchet was set at the measured 78.58% / 64.38% when the Cucumber layer landed, and the campaign has since taken values, rt/Json and rt/StandardLibrary to every line covered. The floor follows the measurement (now 89.30% / 78.95%), so a regression of the equality, hash or range-counting work above — or of any line this tranche covered — fails check instead of quietly reopening the gap.
  • The root AGENTS.md no longer claims that no coverage gate is enforced — the *Test coverage* status said JaCoCo was report-only with nothing enforced; the root build.gradle has since grown a coverageFloors map (eight modules) whose jacocoTestCoverageVerification task check depends on, so a regression below a module's floor does fail the build. The section now separates what is enforced (the per-module floor, raised as coverage improves) from what is not (the 100 % / 0-mutant target itself: PIT runs only for lg3d-mandela, on demand and report-only; Checkstyle runs with ignoreFailures; a module without tests has no floor). The lg3d-mandela test count in *Testing* is corrected with it.
  • Name-resolution tags in the compiler are an enum (Compiler.Ref), not int constants — the load and store switches are now checked for totality by the compiler instead of ending in a guard no script could reach, and a field store lowers itself in storeSlot rather than needing a special case in assign.
  • Operators.div dropped the two conditions it could never need — requireNumbers has already proved both operands are numbers, and Values.isInt *is* instanceof Long, so the isNum(right) ? asLong(right) : 0L fallback and the second instanceof Long test were branches no script could reach and no mutation could kill. The integer path now reads dividend / divisor / exact-or-double.
  • The language guide's LimitError entry covers the library's ceilings too (docs/mandela-language.md) — it named only the step and depth budgets while the standard library had already been raising the kind for repeat and toList sizes; it now says a ceiling, wherever the library enforces one. StandardLibraryTest (270 cases) pins every bullet above and takes rt/StandardLibrary to every line of it covered.

Removed

  • The value surface no receiver can reach (lg3d-mandela, values) — a MandelaIterator was never asked whether it yields pairs or had started, and its index() / source() accessors have no caller in the machine or in a script; the cursor is now one field and one constructor argument. MandelaClass.methods(), declaresField() and visibleMethodNames(), Ref.empty() and the MandelaInstance(owner, initial) constructor are referenced nowhere in the repository — a host builds an instance and assigns its fields, which is what the one-argument constructor already does — and MandelaRange.span() went with the count rewrite above.
  • Ast.BlockValue, an expression node no syntax could produce (lg3d-mandela) — no parser rule ever built it, so the compiler's lowering case, the tree walker's case and the node itself are gone; an expression-bodied function answers through Ast.Stmt.ExprValue, as it already did.
  • StandardLibrary.needList, a guard no script could reach (lg3d-mandela) — a member lookup binds the list vocabulary only to a receiver already matched against MandelaList, and the Range spellings hand over a materialised copy, so the refusal branch was dead code and a mutant no test could kill; the call sites now cast, naming the invariant in the javadoc instead of checking it.

Fixed

  • A lit material's normal and specular maps are bound again — roadmap P2.1, multi-texture (wonderland-renderer) — J3dMeshFactory.buildShaderAppearance resolved a material's normalMapPath/specularMapPath upstream, then bound only the diffuse TextureUnitState and hard-coded hasNormalMap = hasSpecMap = 0, so every lit surface shaded flat off its diffuse and the extra layers were parsed, named and thrown away. The omission was hidden behind a false platform ceiling: WlProbe42 had "measured" this fork as binding exactly one texture per program because a second sampler2D appeared to re-read unit 0 — but the probe set two TextureUnitStates and never assigned the second sampler a unit, and an unassigned GLSL sampler defaults to unit 0. That is a binding bug in the probe, not a limit in the fork. WlProbe48 settled it: three distinct textures (diffuse/normal/spec) render live on one program once each sampler is named on the program (setShaderAttrNames) and assigned its unit through a ShaderAttributeValue(samplerName, unitIndex). buildShaderAppearance now does exactly that — diffuse on unit 0, the normal map on the next unit, the specular mask on the one after, each sampler declared and bound only for a layer whose bytes actually resolved, with hasNormalMap/hasSpecMap set from what resolved so a missing layer stays off and is never sampled unbound. WlProbe49 drove the shipping createShape on the repo's live X:0 / GL 4.6 radeonsi context and measured the fix: a lit facing quad read (255,255,255) on its diffuse and (56,56,56) once a tangent normal map was attached, the map tilting the interpolated normal off the key — identical quads, so the delta is the normal unit binding and sampling, not a lighting change. The default path is untouched: the shader route stays opt-in (-Dlg.wonderland.shader=true), a pre-lit material never asks to be shaded, and a material with no extra layers still binds one unit — so a world whose art carries no normal/spec map draws the pixels it always drew. The retracted ceiling was also corrected where it was cited: ShaderAppearancePlan's GLSL notes and docs/wonderland-roadmap.md (Normal mapping row, Platform ceiling, P2.1, and the P2.5 env basis — which now honestly narrows to "a samplerCube beside a diffuse is unmeasured", not "one texture is the max").

The test reports of a published release are generated beside this page: <version>/reports/ carries the JUnit, JaCoCo, Cucumber and PIT mutation reports of every module with a test suite. Each module runs report-only (mutationThreshold = 0, no gate) unless it appears in the mutationExemptions map, where it is gated at the score its own suite really achieves. The same tree is attached to the GitHub release as reports-<version>.zip, so a report outlives a rebuilt site.
